title: When participation disappears, the underlying problem may not have disappeared
memo: Rivermere 2035 shows that residents routinely absorb service unreliability through private buffers, local knowledge and informal support. Chapel Lane follows the same mechanism under prolonged reporting: residents initially make conditions administratively visible, then withdraw the labour when acknowledgements cannot be connected to an intelligible outcome. Across both projects, a quieter administrative record can coexist with continuing inconvenience because people have left earlier, changed route, moved rooms, relied on others or stopped reporting.
negative_cases_and_limits: CL-E060 distinguishes apparent non-resolution from evidence of no internal work.
CL-E112 retains support for proportionate enforcement alongside criticism of exaggerated resident claims.
R35-E028 shows visible maintenance changing interpretation without erasing earlier communication failure.
R35-E102 records a beneficial aspect of an unwanted travel adaptation.
